newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China, SE Asia soymeal demand explosive - analyst.
newsitem.headline: China, SE Asia soymeal demand explosive - analyst.

text.p: Soymeal demand in China and Southeast Asia will grow at an explosive rate in coming years due to increasing consumption of poultry, pork and beef in the region, a senior analyst said on Monday.

China has gone from exporting 2.41 million tonnes of soymeal in the 1990/91 October/September marketing year to importing an estimated 2.7 million tonnes in the 1996/97 season, John Baize, the president of a U.S.-based oilseeds consulting company, said.
China also imported about 1.7 million tonnes of soybeans in 1996/97 against exports of 1.33 million tonnes in 1989/90.
Another country where growth could suddenly mushroom rapidly is India, where trade liberalisation and rising affluence may well turn the country into an importer of soymeal.
"India promises to be over the next 10 years, the next China as far as soymeal consumption is concerned," Baize said.
Trade liberalisation has lowered tariff barriers on feed and has allowed people "to consume more meat and poultry which stimulates global demand for mixed feeds," Baize said.
Southeast Asian demand has also grown sharply, led by Indonesia and the Philippines, whose combined population reaches around 270 million people, Baize said.
Soymeal imports in the region are expected to hit 3.365 million tonnes in 1996/97 against 989,000 tonnes in 1989/90.
"Now with ASEAN's free trade area, that will even pick up," Baize said in referring to the plan by ASEAN to trim tariffs on a wide range of products to a minimum of five percent by 2000.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

Most of the upsurge in demand has benefited Brazil and Argentina, with Baize estimating that Brazilian farmers will probably export up to seven million tonnes of soybeans this year against 3.5 million tonnes last year.
"The U.S. is not capturing that growth. It has been South America that has captured most of the growth in soybean meal. The place that is responsible for most of that is Asia."
Soybean output in Brazil this year is expected to hit 26.5 million tonnes, while production in Argentina should hit 12.5 million tonnes.

"If you talk to the American soybean farmer or the Brazilian soybean farmer, he's a happy fellow," Baize said, pointing to the recent surge in prices of soybeans and soy products in the Chicago futures market.
